pcs.pc_description: Identify raw materials needed for making Kalamkari painting, including cotton or silk fabric, natural dyes, fixatives (alum), and other natural agents.
Collect raw materials like fabric, natural dyes (derived from vegetables, roots, and minerals), cow dung, natural detergents, and tamarind seed powder in prescribed quantities.
Collect tools such as kalam (bamboo or date palm pen), charcoal or natural ink for sketching, brushes, and containers for dyes.
Prepare the fabric prior to the painting process using tools like scissors, measuring tape, and water containers for soaking.
Prepare natural dyes using raw materials by boiling or grinding the ingredients and ensuring the right consistency of color.

modules.module_title: Perform Kalamkari Painting Process as per the Standard Procedures

pcs.pc_description: Soak the fabric in a mixture of natural bleaching agents like cow dung or bleach for a specified number of days to remove starch and impurities.
Wash and dry the fabric under the sun to achieve a clean, pure base for painting.
Prepare the fabric with natural detergents to achieve the required softness and texture before painting.
Mix alum with water to act as a mordant for fixing the dyes onto the fabric.
Use a bamboo kalam (pen) to sketch designs on the prepared fabric using natural ink or charcoal.
Use a brush or kalam to apply the natural dyes onto the fabric, ensuring that the colors are evenly distributed and absorbed.
Ensure that the application of colors is in line with traditional Kalamkari motifs, ensuring adherence to historical and cultural accuracy.
Allow each layer of color to dry thoroughly before applying the next layer to avoid smudging or blending of colors.
Ensure final drying of the painted fabric under sunlight to achieve the desired vibrancy and finish of the painting.
Perform quality checks to ensure that the design, color application, and finish of the Kalamkari painting meet the required standards.

modules.module_title: Prepare required raw materials

pcs.pc_description: Identify and select the appropriate fabric or base material for Rogan painting, typically cotton, silk, or khadi.
Collect raw materials for making Rogan paint, including castor oil and natural pigments.
Heat castor oil to the required temperature, ensuring it thickens to the right consistency for the Rogan process.
Mix natural pigments into the thickened castor oil to create vibrant Rogan paints.
Collect traditional Rogan painting tools, such as metal styluses (Kalam) for freehand design work.
Prepare the fabric by stretching or securing it on a frame, ensuring the surface is flat and smooth.
Arrange Rogan paints and tools in an organized manner, ensuring easy access during the painting process.

Ensure symmetry in the design by folding the fabric when necessary, allowing the Rogan paint to transfer and mirror the design on both sides.
Layer the Rogan paint carefully, ensuring that each color is applied precisely and without overlapping other elements of the design.
Regularly clean the stylus during the painting process to ensure clean and crisp lines in the artwork.
Allow the painted fabric to air dry fully, ensuring the Rogan paint sets without smudging or cracking.
Perform periodic quality checks to ensure the precision of the patterns and the even application of the Rogan paint across the fabric.

Clean and maintain tools and equipment, ensuring the stylus and other materials are in good condition for future use.
Store the finished Rogan painting in a clean, dry environment to preserve its quality and prevent deterioration over time.

modules.module_title: Prepare the required raw materials and tools

pcs.pc_description: Select an appropriate surface or medium for Mandala art, such as paper, canvas, or fabric, based on the project requirements.
Gather essential drawing tools like pencils, erasers, rulers, compasses, and protractors to create accurate geometric designs.
Choose coloring mediums such as fine-tip pens, colored pencils, markers, or paints that suit the surface and desired effect.
Ensure the availability of stencils or grids if needed to assist in constructing symmetrical and complex patterns.
Set up the workspace in an organized and comfortable manner, ensuring all materials are within easy reach for uninterrupted work.
Prepare the drawing surface by securing it on a stable, flat surface, and ensuring it is clean and ready for detailed work.

modules.module_title: Execute the Mandala Art Creation Process

pcs.pc_description: Establish the center point on the drawing surface, which will serve as the focal point of the Mandala.
Use geometric tools (rulers, compasses, and protractors) to divide the surface into equal sections, ensuring accurate symmetry.
Draw concentric circles and radial lines starting from the center to create the foundational structure of the Mandala.
Add intricate patterns and motifs within each section of the Mandala, ensuring that all elements are proportional and balanced.
Maintain symmetry by ensuring all design elements are consistently spaced and reflect the intended geometry.
Refine the Mandala’s details by adding layers of complex shapes, lines, and symbols according to the design concept.
Ink the design using fine-tipped pens, ensuring the lines are crisp, smooth, and free from smudging.
Apply colors meticulously, following a well- planned color palette, ensuring harmony and contrast between sections.
Use techniques such as shading, blending, and layering to add depth, texture, and a three- dimensional effect to the artwork.
Continuously check for precision, ensuring that the Mandala's design and color application remain balanced and cohesive.

modules.module_title: Post-Creative and Finalization

pcs.pc_description: Review the completed Mandala to check for any inconsistencies, ensuring the design is accurate and the colors are applied evenly.
Ensure the artwork is properly dried or cured, especially if using paint or ink, before handling or packaging.
Protect the finished Mandala, ensuring its preservation and presentation quality.
Safely store completed Mandalas in a suitable environment, avoiding exposure to light, moisture, or dust to preserve their quality.
